lawyer: Enayetur Rahim with Md Alamgir and Md Jahangir Alam, Advocates ------ For the Petitioners.
parties:
Mainuddin Chowdhury & others   ------ Petitioners
Vs.
State and another   ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Aziz J: In this Rule the opposite parties including Kabir Ahmed impleaded as opposite party No.2, were directed to show cause as to why the order dated 25-5-2000 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Chittagong in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1596 of 1999 corresponding to GR No. 132/99 arising out of Satkania PS Case No. 3(7)99 cancelling the bail by the accused-petitioners should not be set aside and also as to why the accused-petitioners should not be enlarged on bail in the said case. 

 3. The prosecution case, in short, inter alia, is that the informant opposite party No. 2 Kabir Ahmed lodged a first information report with Satkania Police Station implicating 32 persons including the present petitioners alleging that on 7-7-99 they forming an unlawful assembly and being armed with deadly weapons, namely, cutrifle, kirich, etc. attacked the house of the informant, at the instruction of accused No. 1 Asabuddin Chowdhury and assaulted one Morshed Ahmed, a cousin of the informant and ransacked his house, looted away the valuables and ornaments of the inmates of the informant, etc. by firing gun shots and injuring others. The case was registered as Satkania PS Case No. 3(7) dated 8-7-99 under sections 147/148/149/447/448/323/324/326/307/427/380 of the Penal Code. On the application of one Md Jamaluddin filed an 20-7-99 before the learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Cognizance Court No. 4, Chittagong, stating that the said injured Md. Morshed Ahmed having died in Chittagong Medical College Hospital during treatment, section 302 of the Penal Code was included in the case the petitioner No. 1 was granted bail by the learned Magistrate on 14-7-99 and the petitioner Nos. 2-4 were granted bail by the same Court on 29-7-99. On an application filed on 29-9-99 by the informant before the learned Sessions Judge for cancellation of the bail of the petitioners granted earlier by he Magistrate as aforesaid, the learned Sessions Judge cancelled the bail on 25-5-2000 of the accused- petitioners and hence this Rule. 

 5.	 Mr M Enayetur Rahim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused- petitioners, submits that the application filed by the informant opposite party No. 2 before the learned Sessions Judge for cancellation of bail of the accused-petitioners was absolutely vague and indefinite and there was no mention of any specific allegation as to on what date and to which witness the alleged threat was made and the police report is also vague and it does not mention any specific incident of threat. The learned Advocate also submits that the learned Sessions Judge did not make any independent opinion of his own on merit of the grounds taken in the application by the informant opposite party No. 2 for cancellation of bail of the petitioners. He also submits that the reply submitted by the petitioners showing cause as directed by the learned Sessions Judge on the application for cancellation of bail, has not at all been considered by the learned Sessions Judge in his impugned order. The learned Advocate further submits that the application for cancellation of bail is motivated and malafide as it was filed after filing of the petition of compromise in the case before the Court and after taking bail of the informant from the Court below in the counter case filed by the petitioner No. 1 on the self-same incident against the informant and others. He also submits that such vague application and vague police report cannot be the basis of cancellation of bail of the petitioners in the admitted facts of enmity and pending of counter cases between the parties. In support of his submission the learned Advocate has cited some decisions in the case between the Government of Sindh through The Chief Secretary, & 4 others vs Haeesa Farooq & 5 others, reported in 1994 SCMR 1283, in the case between Asghar Ali Asad vs Mohammed Ramzan & 3 others, reported in 1984 Pak. CrLJ (Lahore) 384 and in the case between Maqbool Ahmed & another vs State, reported in P CrLJ 1982 (Lahore) 724 in support of his submission. The learned Advocate for petitioners, lastly, submits that although the informant Md Kabir Ahmed has been made opposite party No.2 in this revision and although a Division Bench of this Division has granted bail to accused-petitioners 1-3 vide order dated) 7-8-2000 pending hearing of the Rule, the said informant Md Kabir Ahmed Opposite Party 2 has neither filed any counter-affidavit nor opposed this Rule at any time. 

 6. We have heard the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioners and perused the relevant papers enclosed with the petition vide Annexures A-I series. The first information report of this case lodged by opposite party No.2 on 8-7-1999 at 9 AM has been enclosed as Annexure-A and the first information report lodged by petitioner No. 1 with the said police station on the same date 8-7-1999 at 21-30 hours on the same said occurrence dated 7-7-99 against the aforesaid informant opposite party No. 2 Md Kabir Ahmed and others has been enclosed as Annexure-H and a case was registered as Satkania PS Case No. 2(7)99. From perusal of the aforesaid 2 first information reports, it appears that there had been enmity between the two parties and there was a case and counter-case on the same said occurrence between the parties. In the case before us it appears from the first information report lodged by the informant opposite party No. 2 that, no specific involvement and overt act of the petitioners No. 1-3 was alleged in the first information report except the allegation that they had guns in their hands and that the petitioner No.4 dealt a Kirich blow on the body of deceased Morshid Ahmed who died in Chittagong Medical College Hospital 10 flays after the occurrence during his treatment for which section 302 of the Penal Code was included in the case as stated above. It also appears that petitioner No. 1 was granted bail on 14-7-99 by the learned Magistrate on consideration of the facts of the case and petitioner Nos. 2-4 surrendered before, Magistrate on 21-7-99 and were granted bail by the Court. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioners referring to Annexure-I series submitted that the informant opposite party No. 2 filed an application in the case before the Magistrate stating that the case arose out of misunderstanding between the parties and at the intervention of the respectable local personalities, the dispute has been settled between them. The said opposite party No. 2 has also filed another application before the same Court of the Magistrate on 18-7-99 to the same effect. The learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that when the matter was amicably settled at the intervention of the local personalities between both the parties which is evidence from Annexure-1 series, and taking his own bail thereafter will in the counter case filed by the petitioner No. 1 as stated above, the informant opposite party No. 2 filed the aforesaid application with vague and malafide motive before the learned Sessions Judge for cancellation of bail of the petitioners on vague, fake and frivolous grounds. The said application for cancellation of bail has been marked as Annexure-D. We have gone through the same. The grounds taken in the application alleged that the learned Magistrate did not apply his judicial mind while granting bail to the accused-petitioners and has granted bail to the petitioners also in spite of having specific allegation against them. It has further been alleged in the said application that after taking bail the petitioners have been threatening the informant opposite party No. 2 and other witnesses of the case to withdraw the case or to face dire consequences and dragged the informant holding the collar of his shirt while he came to Court to take steps in the case and that the petitioners have been implicated in the case under section 302 of the Penal Code and they should not have been granted bail. The petitioners have submitted their reply to show cause vide Annexure-F denying the aforesaid allegation categorically and disclosing about the counter-case filed by petitioner No. 1 against informant opposite party No.2 and others on the same set of occurrence as stated above Annexure-E is the police report submitted by the local police before the Magistrate on the aforesaid application for cancellation of bail. In the said report it has been stated that one Md Jamal Uddin, SI of Satkania PS inquired into the allegation brought by the informant Opposite Party No. 2 for cancellation of the bail of petitioners and submitted report dated 27-10-99 finding the allegation as correct. 

 7. We have perused Annexure-D the application for cancellation of bail and Annexure-E the police report submitted on 27-10-99 in the case. It appears from Annexure-D the application for cancellation of bail that the informants opposite party No. 2 has made some general allegations of threat against the petitioners and has not mentioned as to the name of persons to whom such threat was given and the day or dates on which the same was made to the informant or to other witnesses of the case. The application also does not disclose the date on which day the informant opposite party No. 2 was dragged in the Court by his collar and the names of the petitioners who did so. The police report also does not show any specific details substantiating the allegation made in the application for cancellation of bail by opposite party No. 2. The Annexure-P is the reply of the show cause submitted before the Sessions Judge by the petitioners on 25-1-2000 denying the allegation brought by opposite party No. 2 in his application and disclosing other material including the filing of the counter-case by petitioner No.1 against the same opposite party No. 2 on the same said incident which was numbered as Satkania PS Case No. 2(7)99 dated 8-7-99. The learned Sessions Judge cancelled the bail of the petitioners.by his impugned order dated 25-5-2000. On perusal of the said impugned order it appears that the learned Sessions Judge has, in fact, cancelled the bail on taking into consideration of the police report only and did not at all consider the reply submitted by the petitioners before him and on the finding that the case pending against the petitioners was under section 302 of the Penal Code. From the impugned order it further appears that the learned Sessions Judge has not given his independent finding on the allegations made and has not also at all considered the attending facts and circumstances of the case including the facts of enmity and counter case. This is a settled principle of law for the purpose of cancellation of bail on the application of the aggrieved person that the Court cancelling the bail must be satisfied that the grounds taken for cancellation of bail are cogent, specific and sustainable in the facts and circumstances of the case and must rely on a detailed inquiry report and materials. The Court must also take into consideration while cancelling the bail the attending facts and circumstances between the parties including the enmity and the fact of counter-case pending before the same either arising out of the same set of facts and occurrence or otherwise and must not rely on mere police report containing unspecific and general reply. We have gone through the decision in the case between Government of Sindh & 4 others vs Raeesa Farooq and 5 others, reported in 1994 SCMR 1283 wherein it has been held that: 

 "A Court granting bail is empowered to cancel it provided reasonable grounds are made out. In the present case the application made by the appellants alleged that the respondents have jumped the bail and did not attend the investigation whenever called upon to do so. These were vague and general allegations which could be made at any time against any accused. In fact, once bail has been granted the prosecution should make out a strong case for cancellation not by making allegations alone, but by giving substantive proof of such allegations. In the present case the appellants had filed an application which did not give any particulars of any nature. It was an application making general allegations without any attempt to substantiate the same." the learned Judge, therefore, rejected the application." 

 8. In the case between Maqbool Ahmed and another vs State reported in 1982 Pak CrLJ (Lah) (VoI. XV) 724, it has been held that: 

 9. In another case between Asghar Ali Asad vs Muhammad Ramzan & 3 others, reported in 1984 PCrLJ (Lah) 384, a single Bench of the Lahore High Court rejected petition for the cancellation of bail on the ground that "no untoward incident taking place since his release on bail". 

 In the present case as discussed above, the grounds taken by the informant opposite party No.2 have not been substantiated by any proof prima facie to show that the petitioners had, in fact, threatened him or his witnesses as alleged or any untoward act had happened between the parties. In absence of such materials it appears to us that the learned Sessions Judge has wrongly cancelled the bail of the petitioners on the unfounded allegation brought by the informant opposite party No. 2. In the facts and circumstances of the case we find merit in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners and hold that the impugned order passed by the learned Sessions Judge is wrong and illegal and not maintainable in the facts and circumstances of the case.
